'''Kerstin Lindblad-Toh''' is a scientist in [[comparative genomics]], specializing in mammalian genetics. She is the Scientific Director of vertebrate genomics at the [[Broad Institute]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=2015-11-23|title=Kerstin Lindblad-Toh|url=https://www.broadinstitute.org/bios/kerstin-lindblad-toh|access-date=2020-07-12|website=Broad Institute|language=en}}</ref> and a professor in comparative genomics at [[Uppsala University]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Hammar|first=Veronica|title=Lindblad-Toh Kerstin - Department of Medical Biochemistry and Microbiology - Uppsala University, Sweden|url=https://imbim.uu.se/research-groups/genetics-and-genomics/Lindblad-Toh_Kerstin/|access-date=2020-07-12|website=imbim.uu.se|language=en|archive-date=2020-08-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200806134524/https://www.imbim.uu.se/research-groups/genetics-and-genomics/Lindblad-Toh_Kerstin/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2010 she co-founded [[Science for Life Laboratory]] (SciLifeLab) together with [[Mathias Uhlén]] and acted as Co-Director until 2015. As the leader of the Broad Institute's Mammalian Genome Initiative she has led the effort to sequence and analyze the genomes of various mammals, including [[Mus musculus|mouse]], [[dog]], [[Pan troglodytes|chimpanzee]], [[horse]], [[rabbit]] and [[Monodelphis domestica|opossum]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2008-04-30|title=29 Mammals Project|url=https://www.broadinstitute.org/mammals-models/29-mammals-project|access-date=2020-07-12|website=Broad Institute|language=en}}</ref> She has researched extensively on the genetics of [[Dog|dogs]], identifying genes and [[Single-nucleotide polymorphism|genetic variants]] important in disease susceptibility, morphology and behavior.<ref name=":0" />

In 2015, she started the [[Zoonomia#Genomic_Sequence_Alignment_Project|Zoonomia Project]], named after the medical work (1794–96) by [[Erasmus Darwin]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://zoonomiaproject.org/the-project/ | title=The Project – Zoonomia }}</ref>

Lindblad-Toh is elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]] of the United States and the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Naylor |first=David |title=Kerstin Lindblad-Toh new member of National Academy of Sciences - Uppsala University, Sweden |url=https://www.uu.se/en/news/article/?id=14638&typ=artikel |access-date=2022-04-14 |website=www.uu.se |language=en}}</ref>

== Education and early career ==
Lindblad-Toh was born 1970 in [[Stockholm, Sweden]]. She studied [[molecular biology]] as an [[Undergraduate degree|undergraduate]] at [[Karolinska Institute]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Hulth|first=Annica|title=Kerstin Lindblad-Toh - Uppsala University, Sweden|url=https://www.uppsalauniversitet.se/en/news-media/researcher-profiles/kerstin-lindblad-toh/|access-date=2020-07-13|website=www.uppsalauniversitet.se|language=en|archive-date=2020-07-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200713001835/https://www.uppsalauniversitet.se/en/news-media/researcher-profiles/kerstin-lindblad-toh/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 1998, she received her [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] from the Department of Molecular Medicine at [[Karolinska Institute]]. She worked on several projects as a postdoctoral fellow at the Whitehead Institute/MIT Center for Genome Research together with [[Eric Lander]], including mouse SNP discovery, the development of genotyping technologies and association studies in human disease.<ref>[http://www.broadinstitute.org/about/bios/bio-lindblad-toh.html Broad Institute: Kerstin Lindblad-Toh] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716065419/http://www.broadinstitute.org/about/bios/bio-lindblad-toh.html|date=2011-07-16}}, accessed on December 19, 2009</ref> In 2002, she co-authored the paper describing the initial genome sequence of the mouse,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Mouse Genome Sequencing Consortium|last2=Waterston|first2=Robert H.|last3=Lindblad-Toh|first3=Kerstin|last4=Birney|first4=Ewan|last5=Rogers|first5=Jane|last6=Abril|first6=Josep F.|last7=Agarwal|first7=Pankaj|last8=Agarwala|first8=Richa|last9=Ainscough|first9=Rachel|last10=Alexandersson|first10=Marina|last11=An|first11=Peter|date=2002-12-05|title=Initial sequencing and comparative analysis of the mouse genome|journal=Nature|volume=420|issue=6915|pages=520–562|doi=10.1038/nature01262|issn=0028-0836|pmid=12466850|doi-access=free}}</ref> and in 2005 she published the first genome sequence of the domestic dog.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Lindblad-Toh|first1=Kerstin|last2=Wade|first2=Claire M.|last3=Mikkelsen|first3=Tarjei S.|last4=Karlsson|first4=Elinor K.|last5=Jaffe|first5=David B.|last6=Kamal|first6=Michael|last7=Clamp|first7=Michele|last8=Chang|first8=Jean L.|last9=Kulbokas|first9=Edward J.|last10=Zody|first10=Michael C.|last11=Mauceli|first11=Evan|date=2005-12-08|title=Genome sequence, comparative analysis and haplotype structure of the domestic dog|journal=Nature|volume=438|issue=7069|pages=803–819|doi=10.1038/nature04338|issn=1476-4687|pmid=16341006|doi-access=free}}</ref>
